lens_tip: Use the main (1x) lens; switch to 0.5x ultra-wide only for a tight street or to include tall buildings, since it distorts bodies up close.
camera_height_tip: Hold the phone at chest-to-shoulder height for standing/leaning shots; drop to waist height for a slightly heroic, elongated look.
lighting_tip: Overcast skies or the shade side of the street give even, flattering light; avoid harsh midday sun which creates hard shadows on the face.
composition_tip: Place the subject on a vertical third line and use street lines, crosswalks or building edges as leading lines toward them.

lens_tip: Use 0.5x or 1x to include the sea and sky; keep the lens dry and wipe off any salt spray between shots.
camera_height_tip: For full-body shots, hold the phone around waist height and tilt slightly up so the horizon sits in the upper third.
lighting_tip: Shoot at golden hour (just after sunrise or before sunset); try backlighting with the sun behind the person for a soft glow and rim light.
composition_tip: Place the person on a third line, keep the horizon level, and leave open space on the side they are facing or looking toward.

lens_tip: Use 1x or a slight zoom (2x) to compress the background into soft, blurred greenery and flowers.
camera_height_tip: Shoot at or slightly below the subject's eye level to keep flowers and foliage filling the frame behind them.
lighting_tip: Prefer soft, diffused light (overcast or dappled shade under trees); avoid direct sun which can blow out pale petals.
composition_tip: Frame so flowers or leaves fill the foreground or background on at least one side, keeping the face in a clean, uncluttered patch.

lens_tip: Use the main 1x lens; avoid ultra-wide, which will distort the table and cup in the foreground.
camera_height_tip: Shoot from across the table at the subject's eye level, roughly table height, for a natural, candid feel.
lighting_tip: Seat the subject facing a window and shoot with the window light on their face; avoid shooting directly against strong backlight from the window.
composition_tip: Let the cup, book or plate anchor the lower third of the frame, with the subject's face in the upper two-thirds.

lens_tip: Use 0.5x to capture a wide landscape with the subject small within it, or 1x for a closer full-body shot with some background context.
camera_height_tip: For wide, scenic shots keep the phone near eye height and level; for full-body portraits, crouch slightly so the horizon sits mid-frame or lower.
lighting_tip: Golden hour (early morning or late afternoon) gives warm, soft side or back light through trees and foliage.
composition_tip: Use a path, shoreline or tree line as a leading line toward the subject, and keep them off-center on a third line rather than dead-center.
